decisions.node_type: member writes (tm.tm_year = 116;) and member reads on call temporaries (parse_arg_id("42:").res)
decisions.question: M37.9 differential after the deriveCppEdges oracle (CPPD2/CPPD3): member WRITES emitted uses (only the call-callee position was write-gated, not assignment LHS) and member reads on call temporaries were dropped (the obj.type === call_expression guard wrongly treated them as method calls). Aligned to the family member-read contract; fixture stateless-analyzer re-authored to pin the corrected write/read contract.

M37.9 (CPPD5): a comment inside the parameter list broke the signature-exact override match -- all 22 fmt override pairs were missed. Root defect: the analyzer compared full parameter TEXT including parameter names, but names are not part of C++ signatures and a commented-out name disappears entirely. Fixed to a structural TYPE-ONLY signature. Verified 45 -> 56 overrides on gtest.h (Empty's full set now resolves).

M37.9 (CPPD6): recovery-mangled new_expression targets fabricated garbage instantiates edges. A real constructed type is a clean identifier (optionally namespace-qualified); anything else is a recovery artifact and emits no edge (the C-wave CGD19 class).

M37.9 fmt gtest Message ctor (CPPD8): a leading '::' nests an extra qualified_identifier level, so one unwrap left 'std::stringstream' still qualified and the clean-leaf regex dropped the whole edge, while 'new ::Foo' (single unwrap reaches the leaf) worked. Fixed: descend to the innermost name. Differential MISSING 3 -> 0 (5,074-truth floor with headers + calls/uses/instantiates audited); pinned in fixture system-completeness + mutant cpp/drop-global-scope-new.

M37.9 beyond-gates probes: (1) explicit operator calls (unqualified/qualified/member forms) are ERROR-recovered by the pinned grammar -- no call edge is representable; operator DEFINITIONS parse and symbolize correctly. (2) Unqualified calls cannot be ADL-resolved statically (family contract). (3) cpp overrides require virtual-semantics reconstruction and are not independently derivable -- the analyzer's type-only signature resolution is fixture-pinned (override-signature-aware, virtual-override-resolution); overrides are excluded from the differential compared-label set (like csharp/dart/swift) and the truth's same-name heuristic no longer fabricates them.

decisions.node_type: constructor-body call attribution + qualified_calls payload (deep review 2026-09-05)
decisions.question: CPPD9: constructor scopes were pushed under the raw CLASS name while the symbol was normalized to 'constructor', so ctor-body calls emitted source=Engine (the Class symbol) and the qualified_calls payload never reached the constructor symbol. Measured on fmt: 532 ctor-body calls mis-sourced to the Class, 272 class symbols wrongly carrying qc payload. Fix: ctor scope name = normalized symbol name; payload now attaches DIRECTLY to the caller symbolRef (family contract -- groovy/java push at the call site). Verified: 532->203 class-sourced calls (remaining 203 = genuine class-scope initializer/template-deduction call sites, java-family rule: edge from type scope, no symbol payload), class-symbol qc 272->0.

CPPD10: the post-loop #383 payload merge keyed qualified_calls by bare method NAME, so two same-named methods in different classes (Alpha.run / Beta.run) shared one bucket and BOTH symbols carried BOTH classes' call lists. Measured on fmt: 192 method names / 640 excess owners polluted. Fix: direct symbolRef attach at the call site (exact owner) + per-symbol dedupe; runner gained ownerName-aware expectQualifiedCalls and notIncludes assertions so the pollution is pinned both ways.

CPPD11: the virtual registry stored one signature per method name (last-declared wins), so a Derived overriding the FIRST-declared base overload f(int) was silently dropped when Base also declared f(double) -- probe: Derived overriding f(int) AND f(double) emitted one edge. Fix: per-name signature LIST; any matching overload resolves; duplicate (cls.method, base.method) pairs collapse under the no-arity edge model. Discriminating probes pass: override-first-overload, override-second-only, extra-derived-overload-hides.

CPPD12: `using namespace std;` / `using std::vector;` emitted imports in the legacy {source, imported} shape -- the EXACT defect class the C wave fixed for #include (persister reads imp.module, drops module-less imports), so C++ using-imports were never persisted to brain_import. Aligned to the family {module, items} contract (rust use: module = qualified path, items = imported names; namespace form = [*]) + a using_dependency references edge. Class-body `using B::f;` (member re-export) emits nothing -- it is not a module dependency. Pinned in cpp/system-completeness + mutant cpp/legacy-using-import-shape.

CPPD13: call targets leaked template arguments -- `ns::func<int>()`, `s.m<int>()`, `S::m<int>()` emitted targets func<int>/m<int> (855 across fmt). The callee leaf is a template_function/template_method whose text carries the args; the bare name is its first named child. Nested `::` chains (std::numeric_limits<X>::lowest), the `template` disambiguator (dependent_name), defense-parentheses ((X)() -- Windows min/max), functor-temporary invocations (std::forward<F>(f)(args) / Op<int>()(a,b) -- anonymous operator(), CPP-D9) and pointer-to-member recovery ((obj->*pmf)() -- ERROR-recovered, runtime-only callee) all unwrap or suppress to the bare callee. Measured 855 -> 0 leaky/junk targets; full qualified path preserved in the qualified_calls payload. Pinned in cpp/ctor-and-overload-regressions + mutant cpp/template-arg-call-targets.
CPP review (#736): the analyzer emitted NO bare-identifier edges (`return g;` produced zero relationships) while the oracle audited only calls/member reads — a both-sides blind spot.
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED (2026-09-11): file-visible VALUE reads emit Uses with C-family discipline (declaration positions, callee/member leaves, qualified limitation, preprocessor text, labels, attributes, capture bindings, LHS writes, shadowing via walk-order locals, resolvability required); oracle deriveCppBareUses mirrors rule-for-rule. Fixtures cpp/bare-value-reads + mutants cpp/drop-bare-uses, cpp/reemit-shadowed-reads CAUGHT. fmt lanes 0/0/0 both corpora.

decisions.question: CPP review (#736): `TEST(a, b) {...}` parses as function_definition with bare-identifier params — minting TEST symbols per site and resolving reads against macro fiction; bodies' locals also leaked as file-scope symbols and shadow-suppression failed inside bodies.
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED (2026-09-11): ALL-CAPS + typeless-params shapes emit no symbol but walk bodies in an anonymous function scope (locals bind, calls emit globally); oracle pre-pass mirrors the suppression. Fixture cpp/macro-function-shapes + mutant cpp/macro-function-symbols CAUGHT.

decisions.question: CPP review (#736): file-scope `static` functions reported public visibility (exports already excluded via isStatic, so metadata-only) — HC1 parity; in-class static keeps access-specifier visibility (external linkage).
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED (2026-09-11): visibility honors internal linkage; fixture pins (expectVisibility) + mutant cpp/static-fn-public CAUGHT.

decisions.node_type: type reads, qualified reads, macro symbols (limitations)
decisions.question: CPP review (#736): where does bare-read coverage stop? Type positions (`optional<X> y`, `Foo x`), qualified reads (`ns::x`), and preprocessor macro symbols (`#define M` has no symbol) stay silent.
decisions.resolution: DECLARED LIMITATIONS (2026-09-11): types need signature resolution (C-D2 class), qualified reads need cross-scope binding, macro symbols need an extraction pass + oracle work. Each probed (P16/template decls, B7 qualified); silence verified, no fabrication. Revisit as its own wave, never as drive-by expansion.

decisions.question: C++ second review (2026-09-13): an out-of-line definition (`void Foo::bar() {}`) pushes a Method scope named `bar`, so the Class entry that inline methods resolve bare member reads through was absent — `count = count + 1` in Foo::bar emitted nothing on either side (probe-verified shared blindness; lanes stay green by agreement, not by truth).
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED both sides: the function scope carries its class (explicit scope, same key the pre-pass flush uses) and the resolver consults it. Fixture expects add->total (inline/out-of-line parity); mutant cpp/out-of-line-member-silence CAUGHT.

decisions.question: C++ second review (2026-09-13): structured bindings declared nothing — `auto [x, y] = p;` with a file value x emitted uses f->x on both sides (probe-verified shared over-emission).
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED both sides: structured_binding_declarator declares every name (carve-out before the first-only declarator rule; the initializer is a sibling and still reads). File-scope bindings register all names in both pre-passes. Fixture forbids destructure->a (deliberate collision) and expects the post-binding g_alpha read; mutant cpp/structured-binding-reads CAUGHT.

decisions.question: C++ second review (2026-09-13): nested qualification (`Outer::Inner::m`, parsed right-leaning) scoped to the wrong segment on both sides — the analyzer took the outermost qualifier's full text, the oracle the outermost segment — so neither matched the Inner-keyed member registry and bare reads in nested out-of-line bodies stayed silent on both sides.
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED both sides: descend to the innermost qualifier (analyzer getFunctionDetails; oracle pre-pass flush and main-walk class scope, sharing one cleanScope definition). Fixture expects Inner::step->n (source follows the qualified method symbol); mutant cpp/nested-scope-silence CAUGHT.

decisions.question: C++ second review (2026-09-13): a field_declaration or enumerator with a bare identifier value (`int x = LIMIT;`, `A = LIMIT`) has no init_declarator wrapper, so the generic rule treated the VALUE as declaring and the read stayed silent on both sides (probe-verified on both shapes).
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED both sides: segment rule over all children (`,`/`;` split segments fresh, `=`/`:`/`{` switch to reading; first identifier-ish child of a fresh segment declares). Exact for this grammar: `int x = G, y = 2` gives x-declares/G-reads/y-declares, `int x, y;` declares both. Fixture expects Config->LIMIT and Level->LIMIT; mutant cpp/member-init-silence CAUGHT.

decisions.question: M14 #919 (filed from the #743c grammar-leaf round): a call-shaped macro standing as the WHOLE heading of a block. The pinned cpp grammar reads the heading as an `expression_statement` whose terminator is MISSING and leaves the block as a SIBLING `compound_statement` (second spelling: the heading parses as a `function_definition`, the CP2 shape). No `function_definition` ever enclosed the body, so the body was inside NO function scope: its locals published as FILE-SCOPE symbols (5,683 in the two cpp corpora as bare Variables plus 71 under the CP2 spelling), 1,269 of them even became the file's EXPORTS, and every read in the body was sourced at `global` (36 of the 40 body relationships at fmt/test/format-test.cc:2104, 34 of 42 at fmt/test/ostream-test.cc:213). Class size: 193 sites in 14 files of the two cpp corpora (doctest's `SECTION` x169, `TEST_CASE` x7, `TEST` x5), inside the wider `expression_statement > MISSING ";"` class of 411 sites / 67 files. The leak was not confined to the body: a name leaked at file scope made UNRELATED reads elsewhere in the file resolve — nlohmann's unit-regression1.cpp emitted `uses nocopy -> n` at line 113 (the parameter `n` of a class's friend definition) only because the leaked body at line 1365 published a file-scope `n`, and function-local `using` declarations inside a body emitted FILE-SCOPE imports.
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED both sides. `macroDeclaredBody()` (exported from the analyzer) recognises the shape on evidence, not heuristic: the node is a `compound_statement` whose heading sibling is an `expression_statement` carrying a MISSING token and a `call_expression` whose function is an identifier; the analyzer opens a Function scope for the body (context-gated on `enclosingFunctionScope() === null`, because inside a function a call statement followed by a block IS valid C++) and publishes ONE symbol for it: the heading text the source actually writes, flagged `metadata.expandedFrom = "macro-heading"` with `macroName`/`headingText`. Nothing is invented: `TEST(format_test, enum)` generates `format_test_enum_Test::TestBody()`, which appears nowhere in the source, so the heading text is the product decision; the flag keeps consumers from mistaking it for a hand-written function, and the heading is NOT an export (every macro writing this shape gives the generated function internal linkage). The heading text comes from `macroInvocationText()` — paren-group matched with string/comment skipping and line-joins only, REFUSING (no symbol, no scope, old walk) an unreadable heading rather than publishing a damaged name; structural slicing was measured wrong where recovery swallows the body into the argument list (nlohmann's unit-serialization.cpp 169..186). The CP2 spelling now publishes under the same policy (`macroHeadingText`), so both spellings agree. Oracle mirror landed in the SAME commit (script/m14/differential.ts imports `macroDeclaredBody`) per #916's lesson. Evidence: the marker-first 361-file A/B over the two cpp corpora reads 105 files changed, 5,754 leaked file-scope symbols removed / 1,469 headings added, 1,269 leaked exports removed, relationships -35,945/+35,408 with REAL-LOSS 0 in both halves — 34,729 re-attributed, 1,212 re-owned inside a recovered body, 4 phantom targets (a read whose target name was itself a leaked body name), 1 `global`-key hand-off (the dedupe key moved to the next site when the earlier global occurrence acquired an owner). Corpus probes with the recovery live: fmt cpp files=73 tree-truth=5380 covered=5380 (100 %) MISSING=0 analyzer-edges=5168 unexplained=0 heuristic=0; nlohmann-json cpp files=17 truth=1017 covered=1017 (100 %) MISSING=0 edges=1003 unexplained=0. Fixture `cpp/macro-declared-body-919` pins the two heading symbols, forbids the body locals as symbols AND as exports, and forbids the pre-fix `uses … from global` edges; mutant `cpp/macro-declared-body-loss` reproduces the pre-fix output at the result level and is CAUGHT (all 21 cpp mutants caught). Residual, disclosed: where the grammar swallows a heading's own body into its argument list (nlohmann unit-deserialization.cpp `expression_statement [1243..1255]`, whose real body is the sibling at 1256), the region has no scope to derive and reads there fall back to `global` — 1 edge of 35k, kept honest by the same `global` fallback the pre-grammar contract already documents.

decisions.node_type: engine-level (shared c/cpp): the preprocessing in src/ast/engine.ts `parseRaw` blanks a MULTI-LINE `__attribute__(( … ))` / `__declspec( … )` with a space run, which destroyed the newline(s) inside the match and stamped every later node too low by that many rows
decisions.question: M60-C #920, found by the M59 Tier A oracle — the one instrument in this repository that reads a relationship's line claim against the SOURCE rather than against our own tree (so it is the only one that can see a defect both the analyzer and the differential share). On 120 files/lang for c/cpp it read 783 of 38,566 landed relationships naming a line that does not contain the name they claim (c 101 = 1.28 %, cpp 682 = 3.52 %). All of the cpp column traced to one engine line: `parseRaw` blanks compiler extensions before parsing under the comment 'This preserves exact byte bounds and line numbers', and the two patterns `__attribute__\s*\(\([\s\S]*?\)\)` and `__declspec\s*\([\s\S]*?\)` are the only ones in that block that can match ACROSS A NEWLINE — each was replaced with `" ".repeat(match.length)`, so the byte count survived and every `\n` inside the match did not. Proof at one site (zig/lib/libtsan/tsan_rtl.cpp, attribute opened on 51, closed on 52): a raw web-tree-sitter parse of the same bytes reports row 58 for `bool OnFinalize(bool failed);` (written on line 59) while `ASTEngine.parseTree` reported ROW 57. This is cpp's dominant line defect, not c's: c's 101 rows are a different class (the `contains`-onto-a-later-name residue, registered separately in the c spec as C-D10), and c reads 101 before and after.
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED. Both multi-line patterns now blank through `blankKeepingNewlines` (`match.replace(/[^\n]/g, " ")`), so byte offsets (the safety primitives' comment/string-masking contract) and `startPosition.row` are both preserved; the other nine replacements in the same block are literal single tokens whose space run is exactly the pattern's own length (`__restrict__` 12/12, `__restrict` 10/10, `__volatile__` 12/12, `__inline__` 10/10, `__forceinline` 13/13, `__cdecl` 7/7, `__stdcall` 9/9, `__fastcall` 10/10, `__stored_key` 12/12), and a literal without `\n` cannot destroy a row — so the whole block is row-preserving by construction, which is the contract this issue is closed on. Blast radius measured with the engine's own regexes over git ls-files: zig 76 of 14,032 C/C++ files carry a destroyed newline, worst case 138 rows (lib/libc/wasi/libc-bottom-half/sources/__wasilibc_real.c), 340 rows in total; the four pinned corpora contain ONE (fmt/test/gtest/gtest.h). Effect: M59 cpp 682 INCONSISTENT -> 65 on the 120-file draw; on the canonical 40-file draw cpp 41 -> 37 with +5 relationships, all inside the one affected fmt file (the deterministic fmt A/B reads the symbol and relationship PAIR MULTISETS IDENTICAL — 0 names lost, 0 gained — with 2,782 rows moved +1 and 42 unchanged); jq's c and cpp lanes are byte-identical (hashes 2b743b65d0eac283 / 94decf48201d1620 both sides) because that corpus has no multi-line attribute. No existing gate could see this, and that is recorded rather than assumed: the F5 differential's oracle walks the SAME tree as the analyzer (both sides move together and stay MISSING=0), and the M14 fixture runner parses the fixture text itself and calls `analyzer.analyze` directly — only vue/svelte go through the production `parseFile` — so the engine's blanking never runs in that lane at all. The gate therefore lives where the contract lives, and it is registered as `M14.0.F12` (evidence `validation/m14/results/M14.0.F12.json`, claim level L3, layers engine/analyzer/corpus, `--emit` writes it): `script/m14/verify-attr-line-base-920.ts` (`bun run audit:attr-line-base`, wired into `npm run verify`), comparing `ASTEngine.parseTree` against a raw parse of the same bytes keyed by BYTE OFFSET (node TYPES may legitimately differ — blanking removes attributes from the grammar's view — which is why type is never the key), asserting the blanked text keeps the input's byte length, and SELF-TESTING against the pre-fix blanker, which it catches on 13/13 sample files; V0 fails if the sample has no multi-line attribute, so the gate cannot pass vacuously. Fixture `cpp/multiline-attribute-line-base-920` pins the analyzer's own line choices on a file carrying the shape (and that a `contains` edge takes the child's line) while stating that the fixture lane does NOT exercise the engine path, so the two instruments are never confused. Read at the result level, the fix moves lines and nothing else: the A/B over fmt reads the pair multiset identical.

decisions.node_type: contains edges onto a child whose NAME is written on a later line than the child's declaration start (the last M59 Tier A residue, shared with c)
decisions.status: REGISTERED + FILED (#921, a contract question, not a silent gap)
decisions.question: After CP10's fix the M59 Tier A oracle still reads 65 of 24,378 landed cpp relationships (and 101 of 14,188 in c) whose claimed line does not contain the name they claim, and every one is a `contains` edge. The shape is always the same: the child symbol's `range.startLine` is the start of its declaration NODE (the `void`, the `struct`/`union`/`enum`/`typedef` keyword, the `struct {` of an anonymous aggregate) while the name the edge claims is written on a LATER line — `void NORETURN` newline `CheckFailed(…)`, `typedef enum { … } morder;`, `typedef CombinedAllocator<…>` newline `InternalAllocator;`, `struct { … } options;`. Both analyzers set it that way deliberately, documented as 'the edge moves WITH its symbol — the child's own declaration line, so the edge and the symbol range can never disagree (the JVM lesson)'.
decisions.resolution: REGISTERED and FILED as #921 (labels lang:c, lang:cpp), not fixed, because the two readings are different CONTRACTS and the repository already pins the other one for every other edge kind: `cpp/callsite-lines-825` and the M59 oracle require a relationship's line to be the line of the node that NAMES it (implemented for this analyzer's own `references`/`calls`/`extends` through `nameLine`, which prefers the grammar's `name` field), while the symbol's `range.startLine` is deliberately the declaration node's start (fixture `c/callsite-lines-825` pins symbol `seed` at the `struct` keyword's line 31 while pinning `references seed -> Tally` at the name's line 32). So either the `contains` line moves to the NAME (matching the other 7 relationship kinds and the independent oracle), or the child symbol's range narrows to the name line (making edge and range agree, at the cost of moving symbol ranges that search, edit anchors and the M73 line base read). Measured so the decision can be made on numbers rather than taste: 65 cpp rows on the M59 120-file draw, 37 on the canonical 40-file draw (cpp only; c 0 there). No name is lost and every edge and symbol is present and correctly attributed — only `line_number` disagrees with the name-on-line rule.
